deep.reconstruction:
The page is a scratch sheet. Its main thread is the iteration of a linear fractional (Möbius) map. This map arises as the 'tail' recursion of a continued fraction with constant (or limiting-constant) partial quotients. Riemann studies it by conjugating the map to a pure dilation through its two fixed points. A marginal note restates the Dirichlet principle.

(A) Continued-fraction recursion (top centre). The struck numerator should be read as αx, so the recursion is p_m = αx / (1 + ρx/(1+p_{m+1})). Clearing gives p_m = (1+p_{m+1}) αx / (1+p_{m+1}+ρx). Hence p_m/(αx) = 1 − ρx/(1+p_{m+1}+ρx) = 1 − 1/(1/(ρx) + 1 + p_{m+1}/(ρx)). He then tries to put the recursion for p_m^{-1} into the same shape. The partly cancelled lines show a form like −αρ/(1/x + ρ + γ + c·p_{m+1}^{-1}). Either way, p_m = T(p_{m+1}) with T a Möbius map in p_{m+1} whose coefficients depend on x.

(B) The iteration problem. Left column: f(x) = α + γ/(β+x) is the general such map after normalisation. The line read as 'f(x) = α f(f(x))' is most plausibly φ(x) = α φ(f(x)). That is the eigenfunction (Schröder-type) equation for iterating f. Fixed points come from x = f(x), a quadratic. He starts with (x−α)(x−β) and x² − (α+β)x + αβ = 0, then strikes them. Instead he names the two fixed points γ and δ. He introduces the cross-ratio coordinate y = (x−γ)/(x−δ), whose inverse is x = (δy−γ)/(y−1); this is correct.

(C) Normal form with prescribed fixed points (bottom half). Polynomial division gives (x² − (γ+δ)x + γδ)/(x+β) = x − (β+γ+δ) + (β+γ)(β+δ)/(x+β). The remainder is γδ + β(β+γ+δ) = (β+γ)(β+δ). So the map f(x) = β+γ+δ − (β+γ)(β+δ)/(x+β) satisfies x − f(x) = (x−γ)(x−δ)/(x+β). It is thus the general Möbius map with fixed points γ, δ and pole −β. Substituting x = (δy−γ)/(y−1) gives f = (β+γ+δ) − (β+γ)(β+δ)(y−1)/(δy−γ+β(y−1)). The denominator equals (β+δ)y − (β+γ), exactly as written. The last scribbles start converting this back to the y-coordinate.

Completion (mine): f = (δ(β+δ)y − γ(β+γ))/((β+δ)y − (β+γ)). Hence (f−γ)/(f−δ) = ((β+δ)/(β+γ))·y. So in the y-coordinate the map is multiplication by k = (β+δ)/(β+γ), and y_m = k^m y_0. The iterates converge to the attracting fixed point, or fail to converge when |k| = 1. This is precisely the convergence criterion for limit-periodic continued fractions.

(D) A second parametrisation (right-centre). He writes y = (x+β−ρ)/(x+α−ρ), i.e. fixed points ρ−β and ρ−α. He correctly rearranges this as (ρ−x−α)y = ρ−x−β. He then states (f(x)+β−ρ)/(f(x)+α−ρ) = (β/α)·y, i.e. multiplier β/α. Alongside, he writes f(x) = ρ − αρ(y−1)/(ρy−α) and computes (αρ(y−1) − α(ρy−α))/(αρ(y−1) − ρ(ρy−α)) = (α² − αρ)/((αρ − ρ²)y) = α/(ρy). This equals (f+α−ρ)/f for that f, i.e. the same dilation structure for a map with fixed points 0 and ρ−α. The exact link between the variables in these scattered lines is not fully recoverable.

(E) The line α_{2m+1} = b_{2m} − a_{2m}/α_{2m−1} is the general (non-constant) tail/ratio recursion of a continued fraction. Steps (B)–(D) are the constant-coefficient model of it.

(F) Top-right German note: '∫(∂z/∂x)² hat nothwendig einen kleinsten Werth U, u. für eine solche Function für z [ist] V = U.' This is a statement of the Dirichlet principle: the integral necessarily has a minimum value U, attained for some admissible z. It continues the variational discussion of the previous page (boundary conditions, plate problem).

Context: the material fits Riemann's posthumous work on the continued-fraction expansion of quotients of hypergeometric series (Werke, ed. Schwarz). There the asymptotic convergence of Gauss's continued fraction reduces to a limit-periodic continued fraction governed by the fixed points of a Möbius map.
errors: The line transcribed 'p_m = 1/(1+ρx/(1+p_{m+1}+ρx))' cannot equal the next line (1+p_{m+1})αx/(1+p_{m+1}+ρx). The consistent reading is p_m = αx/(1+ρx/(1+p_{m+1})); the extra ρx in the inner denominator is a copying slip (or mistranscription) from the following line.
In the computation (α²−αρ)/(αρ−ρ²y), the denominator should be (αρ−ρ²)·y = ρ(α−ρ)y, since the αρ terms cancel. Read literally as 'αρ − ρρ y' it is wrong; the intended simplification is α/(ρy).

The first attempt at the fixed-point quadratic, (x−α)(x−β) and x²−(α+β)x+αβ=0, does not correspond to x = α+γ/(β+x); the correct quadratic is x²+(β−α)x−αβ−γ=0. Riemann struck it out and switched to naming the fixed points γ, δ directly.

The relation (f+β−ρ)/(f+α−ρ) = (β/α)y is not consistent with the f(x) = ρ − αρ(y−1)/(ρy−α) written beside it if both use y = (x+β−ρ)/(x+α−ρ). The lines appear to belong to different trial parametrisations; this is not a substantive error but they cannot be combined as written.
The final line (y²+1)(β+δ)(β+γ) − y(β+γ)²(β+δ) is an unfinished, apparently abandoned expansion; it does not follow from the preceding lines as written.

results.what: Tail recursion of a continued fraction p_m = αx/(1+ρx/(1+p_{m+1})) rewritten as a Möbius map of p_{m+1}
results.modern_name: Tails of a (limit-)periodic continued fraction as iterates of a linear fractional transformation
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange, Galois (periodic continued fractions); systematic convergence theory by Pringsheim, Van Vleck and Perron (c. 1900)

results.what: Conjugating a Möbius map with fixed points γ, δ to a dilation via y = (x−γ)/(x−δ), with multiplier (β+δ)/(β+γ) (resp. β/α)
results.modern_name: Normal form / Schröder linearisation of a loxodromic or hyperbolic Möbius transformation; multiplier of a fixed point
results.usually_credited_to: Babbage (1815) and Herschel for iterating linear fractional functions; Möbius; Schröder (1870) for the general functional equation φ(f(x)) = sφ(x)

results.what: Writing the eigenfunction equation φ(x) = α φ(f(x)) for iteration of f
results.usually_credited_to: Ernst Schröder 1870–71 (with antecedents in Babbage 1815 and Abel)

results.what: General Möbius map with prescribed fixed points γ, δ and pole −β: f(x) = β+γ+δ − (β+γ)(β+δ)/(x+β), with x − f(x) = (x−γ)(x−δ)/(x+β)
results.modern_name: Möbius transformation determined by its fixed points and pole
Backward/forward recurrence for continued-fraction tails (ratio of consecutive convergent denominators)

results.what: Existence of a minimising function for ∫(∂z/∂x)² (note in German)
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet/Gauss/Thomson; named and used by Riemann (1851, 1857)

deep.surprise_reason: Iteration of linear fractional maps by conjugation to a dilation through the fixed points is classical (Babbage, Herschel, Möbius). It is also exactly what Riemann's known posthumous work on hypergeometric continued fractions requires, and the Dirichlet principle is famously his. The only slightly notable item is the explicit Schröder-type equation φ(x) = αφ(f(x)), which predates Schröder (1870). Even so, it appears only for the Möbius case, where it is elementary and has antecedents in Babbage.
